paper_id: Recursive Self-Improvement of Predicates for Skill Routing via Minimum Bayes Risk Replay and Held-out Gates
review_type: Independent presentation, figure and physical/policy compliance audit; not a full scientific review

venue_context.paper_type_basis: Delegated assumption: long research review paper, 8 content pages

headline_verdict: The immutable PDF is physically well formed: 31 total pages but 8 content-bearing pages, with all 8 figures inspected. The main presentational weaknesses are incomplete figure semantics, a backbone-ceiling overclaim, and copy-editing/label-size defects, not an overlength or unembedded-font violation. Venue-specific submission compliance remains conditional on the unknown target and stage.

presentation.justification: Clean layout and recoverable method, offset by ambiguous main captions, small downstream chart labels and grammar defects.

figure_quality.justification: All eight figures render and carry interpretable evidence; statistics, normalization and cost scopes need main-caption clarification.

narrative.justification: Predicate→replay→gate thesis is recoverable and Figure 2 conveys it; Figure 1 is motivation only, and Section 7.3 overstates its three-backbone comparison.

confidence.justification: All 31 pages rendered/text-checked; all eight figures inspected at detail scale; source anchors/hash manifest verified. No fresh experiments, style-file provenance comparison, portal or venue/cycle validation.

confirmed_physical_properties.line_number_note: Rulers accompany prose; float-only pp29–31 have page numbers but no prose rulers. This is not a failure of review mode.
confirmed_physical_properties.title_and_author_metadata: Anonymous author metadata; PDF title omits the word Replay from the rendered title. No identity leak observed.

conditional_policy_assessment.template_note: Observed class/mode and physical layout match ACL review expectations; official acl.sty byte provenance was not compared here. Snapshot immutability is separately verified.
conditional_policy_assessment.anonymity: No observed PDF identity leak; supplements and author history remain unverified.
conditional_policy_assessment.ai_acknowledgment: Allowed by fresh ARR authorchecklist; do not flag it as an anonymity violation.
conditional_policy_assessment.ai_disclosure_adequacy: needs_human_check: current CFP requires scope in Responsible NLP Checklist and details in acknowledgments. Existing p8 statement is generic; actual use, checklist entry and sufficiency cannot be verified from PDF alone.
conditional_policy_assessment.ethics: Relevant corpus/model licenses, sensitive external-service data, medical non-validity and untrusted skill execution are discussed on p8; this is not proof of license or privacy compliance.

location.quoted_text: Retention of required skills averaged across retrievers: BM25, Vector, and SkillSight.

additional_anchors.quoted_text: This is a ratio of task-averaged recalls, rather than an average of task-level retention ratios.
Each method is normalized by its own Recall@50. In particular, SkillDAG expands its initial retrieval set, so its normalization uses the expanded ranked pool.

issues.problem: The headline retention figure does not define its ratio-of-mean-recalls denominator or disclose that SkillDAG uses its own expanded pool in the main caption.
reasoning_chain: 1. Figure 3 plots all methods at 100% for k=50; the caption describes retention but provides no formula.
2. Appendix F.1, p20, defines a ratio of task-averaged recalls and method-specific Recall@50; this is not mean per-task retention or a shared-pool controlled comparison.
3. Because the abstract headline is 90.5% retention, the exact quantity is load-bearing main-paper information rather than merely replication detail.

required_inputs: Existing cited source passages and values; no new experiment required
acceptance_criteria: Main paper defines ratio of mean recalls, not mean task-level ratios.
